Four explanations are offered around the council table: the fare cut to a dollar; the new route out to the county hospital; the parking charge brought in downtown; and the move of the high school to the north end. The counts are for the fare: riding rose in the month the dollar fare began. The hospital route was cut to one morning trip in 2009 and has carried almost nobody since. No name is signed in the log, the depot assigning its buses by ticket instead. No weather note is marked in the log, since rain and ice are recorded elsewhere.

Lifting the parking charge was tried in 2018, and nobody stopped riding. Moving the high school back was tried in 2019, and nobody stopped riding. The finding is proved, and I say so flatly. Four explanations are given in the literature: that the parts were never engraved; that the publisher's warehouse fire destroyed the stock; that Halloway's review frightened the quartets off the programmes; and that the players found the third movements unplayable. Holding Halloway's review back until 1927 was managed by his editor, and no society took them up. Easing the third movements was done by Verrall herself in 1911, and no society took them up. My admiration for Redmond is complete: he read every membrane twice. I have no impatience with Redmond, who finished in three years what nine would have excused.
